differences: Q01 is dominated by 90.2 Hz and a 30.1 Hz-spaced family, whereas R01 is dominated by 45.9 Hz and has a markedly different broadband PSD; the baseline distance is the largest at 4.817 dB.
R01 has strong 4–16 kHz envelope modulation near 61.7/30.9 Hz, while Q01 shifts the 4–8 kHz maximum to 182.2 Hz and the 8–16 kHz maxima to 90.2/60.2 Hz.
R01 shows a 2.08–2.22 s level disturbance and large DC offset; Q01 has no detected level changes.
similarities: Both contain low-frequency harmonic/modulation structure and persistent higher-frequency tonal bands.

differences: R02 is dominated by 45.1 Hz with strong 15/30 Hz-related modulation; Q01 is instead dominated by 90.2 Hz with a coherent 30.1 Hz family extending through 571.5 Hz.
The 4–8 kHz envelope differs strongly: R02 peaks at 91.7 Hz with large normalized modulation, while Q01 peaks at 182.2 Hz with much weaker modulation.
R02 has much lower broadband crest factor and lower spectral centroid than Q01.
similarities: Both have stationary, unclipped recordings and approximately 30 Hz harmonic/modulation components.
Among references, R02 is relatively close in persistence and envelope-band distances, but those controls are not acceptance evidence.

differences: R03 is dominated by 45.0 Hz with prominent 15 Hz modulation across several carrier bands; Q01 is dominated by 90.2 Hz, and its strongest broadband modulation is 30.1 Hz.

Cyclic evidence conflicts strongly: the query-to-R03 cyclic distance is 0.01764, far larger than for every other reference.
similarities: The baseline PSD distance is moderately low at 3.329 dB, and both show approximately 30/60/90 Hz families.

differences: R04 is dominated by 44.9 and 74.8 Hz, whereas Q01 is dominated by 90.2 Hz and lacks the same 44.9/74.8 Hz balance.
R04's 4–8 kHz envelope peaks strongly at 30.4 Hz; Q01 peaks at 182.2 Hz and is much less strongly modulated in that band.
Q01 has a localized spectral-kurtosis peak of 3.04 near 1.06 kHz, versus R04's maximum of 0.51.
similarities: R04 is close in several descriptive controls: cepstrum, cyclic, modulation map, estimators, reassigned STFT, and physical STFT.
Both show persistent harmonic structure near multiples of 30 Hz.

differences: R05 is dominated by 43.9 Hz, with a 29.3 Hz family; Q01 is dominated by 90.2 Hz with 30.1 Hz spacing.
R05 has exceptionally strong 29.9–30.0 Hz modulation in the 4–8 kHz band, while Q01's maximum there is 182.2 Hz.
R05 has no query-like spectral-kurtosis spike near 1.06 kHz; its maximum is only 0.515.
similarities: Both have strong approximately 30 Hz periodic structure and steady, unclipped waveforms.

differences: Although R06 is the nearest baseline PSD control at 3.003 dB, R06 is dominated by 44.9 Hz with a strong 29.9 Hz component, whereas Q01 is dominated by 90.2 Hz.
R06 has strong 15 Hz modulation in the 100–500 Hz and 8–16 kHz bands; Q01 instead emphasizes 120.3/90.2 Hz and 90.2/60.2 Hz, respectively.
R06 shows numerous detected level increases; Q01 has no detected level changes.
Q01's localized 1.06 kHz spectral-kurtosis maximum of 3.04 is absent from R06, whose maximum is 0.60.
similarities: This is the forced nearest baseline reference, and both contain extensive approximately 30 Hz-spaced harmonic families.
Their broad STFT/PSD shapes are more alike than Q01 versus R01, but nearest-reference status alone does not establish similarity.

decision.explanation: Outcome is different: no supplied condition has known similarity sufficient for acceptance. Initial priorities were the condition-distinguishing low-frequency FFT/harmonic families, band-envelope modulation, PSD/STFT shape, and impulsiveness measures. The decisive query evidence is its dominant 90.2 Hz line, coherent approximately 30.1 Hz family, 120.3/90.2 Hz low-band modulation, 182.2 Hz 4–8 kHz modulation, and localized kurtosis anomalies near 1.06 kHz and 7.5–8.7 kHz [Q01.C01.S0001, D07.harmonics, D07.envelope_1, D07.envelope_4, D07.spectral_kurtosis, D07.kurtosis_bank]. Every reference instead has a principal line around 43.9–45.9 Hz and a materially different modulation/impulsiveness pattern. Numerical controls conflict: R06 is nearest in baseline PSD, R04 is nearest in several STFT/modulation controls, R08 is nearest in cepstrum, and R02 is nearest in persistence; no single reference is consistently close. Measurements, rather than image-pixel estimates or forced nearest ranking, drive the rejection. Order spectra and synchronous averages are unavailable for Q01 and all references because no independent RPM trace was supplied [D07.orders, D07.synchronous, R01.orders, R01.synchronous, R02.orders, R02.synchronous, R03.orders, R03.synchronous, R04.orders, R04.synchronous, R05.orders, R05.synchronous, R06.orders, R06.synchronous, R07.orders, R07.synchronous, R08.orders, R08.synchronous]. Consequently, speed/order-based fault identity cannot be tested. The evidence supports outside-reference difference, not a diagnosis, component attribution, or severity claim.
